title: Caption and measurement chips come in a set of professional styles you pick from, like arrow styles
goal: The label chip on arrows and measurements is one look today: a dark pill in the arrow's colour with a coloured outline. Give it a small set of premade, professional chip styles to pick from the same way arrow styles are picked (a row of picture tiles). Not every style is a pill: some are squircles or soft rectangles, some are flat and some are glass with a subtle inner border, and every one looks like it belongs in a polished Mac app or a professional design spec, never like a home-made web page. The chosen style applies to the text chip of that arrow or measurement and can be changed any time without losing the words or colour.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-24 (picture: queue/audits/2026-10-24-user-caption-chip.png, a dark red pill with a brighter red outline reading 'hi' at the tail of a brush arrow): 'I don't love the style of the chip for arrows and measurements. I would love to have some style options for the chip, just like we have for the arrow, where you can choose different premade professional looking chips for typing text. Some might not be pills, maybe we do squirqle shaped, or the border might be more glass like with a suble inner border. Maybe some are flat and others are glass like. Each option should look professional and not like a kid made it for his myspace.'

Where: the plate rule is Sources/PhotonzCore/LabelPlate.swift (tone darkened to luminance 0.24, white ink, shadow 4 blur / 2 offset); drawn by Sources/PhotonzRender/PillRasterizer.swift; also used by canvas name chips (Sources/Photonz/CanvasComponents.swift), which must NOT change unless the runner decides on purpose and logs why. Arrow style pattern to copy: Sources/PhotonzCore/ArrowStyle.swift (enum, Codable, standard default) + Sources/Photonz/ArrowStyleTiles.swift. Grep captionChipColor for the caption's colour path. Measurement readouts sit on their caliper with no shadow (LabelPlate comment): a style must fit both.

Traps: glass over a picture renders differently on canvas (live material) than in export (no backdrop); the export must look the same, so glass is probably drawn as a rendered blur of the picture under it in PhotonzRender, not a SwiftUI material. The coloured outline in today's chip is part of what the user dislikes; do not keep it as the default without a reason. Related done tasks: arrow-tool-captions-legible-pill-labels-like-the, captions-are-one-layer-positioned-and-styled-lik.
acceptance: A chip style picker sits next to the arrow style tiles (and in the measure tool's options), showing each style as a picture tile of a real chip, same pattern as ArrowStyleTiles

Ships at least five styles, for example: the current solid pill; a flat squircle (continuous corners) with no outline; a soft rectangle with a hairline border; a glass chip (translucent material, subtle inner light border, soft shadow); and a light 'paper' chip (light plate, dark text) for dark pictures. The runner may change the set but each must be clearly different from the others, not colour swaps

Every style keeps the label legible over any picture: text to plate contrast is at least 4.5:1 over white, black, a busy photo and a saturated colour, MEASURED for every style and written in the audit (glass styles must still read; LabelPlate's rule that the plate carries legibility still holds)

The style is non-destructive data on the layer, saved in the document, carried by export (the exported chip matches the canvas pixel for pixel within a small tolerance, measured), undoable in one step, and an older document opens in today's style

A visual bar today's chip fails: a side by side sheet of every style on a light, dark and photo background is judged by a model judge against references from Apple's apps, Figma/Sketch redline plugins and CleanShot X, and each style must score as professional; the current red pill with its bright outline is scored on the same sheet as the baseline
The agent can set a chip style through the same command (MCP), and Ask uses it
Try path: open a screenshot at Next defaults, draw an arrow, type a caption, pick each chip style; do the same on a measurement

Audit under queue/audits/ with the style sheet, the contrast table and the export comparison; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not
